questions.prompt: Is repair equivalent to saying sorry?
questions.answer: No; correction and prevention may be needed.

questions.prompt: What if the issue is a structural access barrier?
questions.answer: Change the relevant group process rather than relying on apology alone.
No; the affected person retains choice.
Use appropriate formal or specialist support, prioritising safety.
questions.feedback: Do not insist on direct confrontation.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only; use answer-specific feedback.
scoring.practice: Designs feasible community repair addressing actual impact, process changes, autonomy and appropriate escalation.
scoring.transfer: Complete the community plan: recurring opportunities, reciprocal support and obligations, inclusive invitations and a repair pathway. Include an access barrier, consent and refusal, a structural improvement and a contrasting case requiring formal support.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
